summary: The reader is an undergraduate computer scientist: asymptotic notation and recurrences, discrete mathematics (sets, products, permutations, modular arithmetic, the Chinese remainder theorem, logarithms, floor and ceiling), and introductory linear algebra (matrices, bases, subspaces, inner products, norms, Kronecker products). They know polynomials, complex numbers and roots of unity, basic Turing machines with tapes, and sorting and divide-and-conquer. They have not studied FFT-based multiplication in depth, abstract ring theory beyond basics, numerical error analysis, or any research on integer multiplication complexity.

known.name: Linear maps and matrices
known.gloss: A linear map between finite-dimensional vector spaces is represented by a matrix, and an invertible one has an inverse that undoes it.

known.name: Subspaces, bases and dimension
known.gloss: A subspace is a subset of a vector space closed under addition and scaling, described by a basis whose size is its dimension.

known.name: Tensor (Kronecker) product of vectors and matrices
aliases: product of operators on separate coordinates
known.gloss: The tensor product of vectors or operators acts on a multi-index array by applying one factor along each coordinate axis.

known.name: Vector norms and the sup norm
known.gloss: A norm measures vector size, the sup norm is the largest absolute entry, and a map that never increases the norm is a contraction.

known.name: Inner product and orthogonality
known.gloss: An inner product gives lengths and angles, and two vectors are orthogonal when their inner product is zero.

known.name: Triangular matrices and permutation matrices
known.gloss: Triangular matrices have zeros on one side of the diagonal and are easy to apply and invert, and permutation matrices reorder coordinates.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Integers taken modulo m are identified when they differ by a multiple of m, and addition and multiplication respect this.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, residues modulo each one determine a unique residue modulo their product.

known.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
known.gloss: A prime has no divisors except 1 and itself, and two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1.

known.name: Cyclic groups and indices mod m
known.gloss: The integers mod m under addition form a cyclic group, used to index arrays that wrap around.

known.name: Finite field F_2 and XOR
known.gloss: Bits under addition mod 2 form a field, where addition is the exclusive or.

known.name: Bit operations and address fields
known.gloss: Array indices written in binary split into contiguous fields of bits that can be read, swapped or masked.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijection of a finite set onto itself, and applying one to an array rearranges its entries.

known.name: Cartesian products and multidimensional arrays
known.gloss: A multidimensional array is indexed by tuples from a product of finite sets, one set per axis.

known.name: Floor, ceiling and logarithms
known.gloss: Floor and ceiling round down and up to integers, and the base-2 logarithm gives the number of bits needed for a number.

known.name: Powers of two and dyadic rationals
known.gloss: A dyadic rational is an integer divided by a power of two, exactly representable as a finite binary fraction.

known.name: Rings and the identity y^r = -1
known.gloss: A ring has addition and multiplication obeying the usual laws, and quotienting polynomials by a relation such as y^r=-1 gives a new ring.

known.name: Recurrences and recursion cost analysis
known.gloss: The cost of a recursive algorithm is bounded by solving a recurrence that relates the cost on size n to costs on smaller inputs.

known.name: Sorting and sequential scans on tapes
known.gloss: Sorting arranges items by key in O(N log N) comparisons, and a scan reads a tape once from end to end.

known.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: Grade-school multiplication takes quadratic time in the number of digits, and Karatsuba lowers the exponent by splitting numbers in two.

known.name: Symbols for asymptotics: Theta and Omega
known.gloss: Theta gives a tight order of growth, Omega a lower bound, and tilde notation hides logarithmic factors.

known.name: Real and imaginary parts, conjugates and modulus bounds
known.gloss: A complex number splits into real and imaginary parts, and its modulus obeys the triangle inequality.

known.name: Gaussian function and Gaussian integers
known.gloss: The Gaussian function exp(-pi x^2) is the bell curve, and Gaussian integers are complex numbers with integer real and imaginary parts.

known.name: Subsets, binomial counts and combinatorial counting
known.gloss: Counting the number of ways to choose a subset of given size uses binomial coefficients.

known.name: Fixed finite alphabet and worst-case time
known.gloss: Worst-case time is the maximum number of steps over all inputs of a given length.

known.name: Linear independence and rank
known.gloss: A set of vectors is independent if none is a combination of the others, and the rank counts independent rows or columns.

known.name: Cyclic and negacyclic indices as polynomial wrap
known.gloss: Reducing a polynomial modulo x^n-1 folds high powers back onto low ones, giving cyclic indexing.
